text:
lee-peopleops: Quick question  traveled to Seattle last weekend and my partner had to get taken by ambulance to an ER. We just got the EOB and carrier marked everything as out-of-network and applied full charges. Does our Redwood plan cover emergency care when you're out of state?

andrew-hr: Short answer: yes, emergency services are covered regardless of network in most cases. The carrier should process ER as in-network for true emergencies. You'll need to file an appeal if they paid $0.

lee-peopleops: Ugh the hospital sent a huge itemized bill. The EOB lists reason: "Non-covered - provider not in network" and code: "Ambulance G0390". Do ambulance codes complicate it?

benefits-bot: Filing steps for emergency OON claims: 1) Upload EOB PDF, 2) Upload itemized hospital and ambulance bills, 3) Attach ER discharge summary or physician note describing emergency condition, 4) Include transport/EMS report if available, 5) Member ID and claim number. Appeals must be started within 90 days of EOB date. Portal: https://benefits.redwood.com/claims -> "Submit appeal". Email option: benefits@redwood.com with subject line: "Appeal: OON ER/EMS claim - MEMBER_LASTNAME - DOS 2026-03-08".

tara: The ambulance code won't prevent coverage for emergency stabilization. The EMS report + discharge summary are the key docs. If the provider billed as totally out-of-network, we can ask the carrier to apply "prudent layperson" emergency standard.

andrew-hr: I can open a company-supported appeal. Lee, can you DM me the carrier claim # and upload the PDFs to the portal? I'll chase the carrier phone line and note it's an emergency.

lee-peopleops: Thanks. One more: should I ask the hospital to send a corrected bill with a network billing contact? They mentioned they only have an out-of-network billing office.

benefits-bot: Helpful: request an itemized bill and a billing contact. Also ask hospital to include provider NPI and taxonomy. If they refuse to adjust network status, the carrier can still process emergency services as in-network for payment purposes.

lee-peopleops: Uploading docs now. Claim#: 1122334455. DMing Andrew. Appreciate the help :pray:

andrew-hr: Got it. I'll escalate after you upload. If carrier denies after appeal, we can request an external review with the WA insurance commissioner (since care was in WA). Keep all receipts and notes.

tara: FYI if ambulance vendor tries balance billing, we can also send a balance billing dispute template. Ping me and I'll attach it.

lee-peopleops: Will do. Thanks everyone
